2609.02396.title: Improving Health Literacy through Lay Summarization of Radiological Reports: An Evaluation of BioNER and Retrieval-Augmented Generation
2609.02396.paper_summary: Radiology reports are written primarily for clinicians, and their specialized terminology often makes them difficult for patients to interpret. As a result, many patients turn to publicly available Large Language Models (LLMs) to help explain their reports, despite well-documented risks of factual inaccuracies and hallucinations. Automated lay-summary generation has emerged as a promising alternative, yet the effectiveness of retrieval-enhanced and clinically informed approaches for radiology-specific communication remains underexplored. This study investigates the extent to which Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) and Named Entity Recognition (NER) improve the quality, factual consistency, and readability of automatically generated lay summaries compared with standard LLM-based generation. We develop a framework combining NER-based extraction of clinically relevant findings with a RAG mechanism for contextual grounding, evaluated across few-shot and fine-tuned variants of two models (Qwen, BioBART). Results show that NER consistently improves readability and overall quality, while RAG alone offers no benefit and can introduce hallucinations from irrelevant retrieved terms. Combining RAG with NER degrades performance in few-shot settings but improves readability when fine-tuned. Fine-tuned BioBART with NER achieves the best overall performance, highlighting entity-aware extraction as the primary driver of improved patient-friendly summaries.
2609.02396.paper_summary_zh: 放射科報告主要是為臨床醫生撰寫的，其專業術語往往使患者難以理解。<lb/>因此，許多患者轉向公開可用的大型語言模型（LLMs）來幫助解釋他們的報告，儘管已經有充分的文獻記錄了事實不準確和幻覺的風險。<lb/>自動化的通俗摘要生成已成為一種有前景的替代方案，但針對放射科特定溝通的檢索增強和臨床知識驅動的方法的有效性仍然未被充分探索。<lb/>本研究調查了檢索增強生成（RAG）和命名實體識別（NER）在提高自動生成的通俗摘要的質量、事實一致性和可讀性方面的程度，與標準的基於LLM的生成進行比較。<lb/>我們開發了一個框架，將基於NER的臨床相關發現提取與RAG機制進行上下文基礎的結合，並在兩個模型（Qwen、BioBART）的少量樣本和微調變體中進行評估。<lb/>結果顯示，NER始終改善了可讀性和整體質量，而僅使用RAG則沒有任何好處，並且可能會引入來自不相關檢索術語的幻覺。<lb/>在少量樣本設置中，將RAG與NER結合會降低性能，但在微調時可改善可讀性。<lb/>微調的BioBART與NER結合達到了最佳的整體性能，突顯了以實體為中心的提取是改善患者友好摘要的主要驅動因素。
